answer: Peer-verified work credits, not raw account count, decide voting weight, and unused credits expire after 14 days. Two established, non-kin reviewers must sign each completed task before a credit posts. A farm that unleashes a gale of empty personas stalls on a barren knoll: with no accepted history it cannot vote, and fabricating a tundra of dummy jobs still means paying those reviewers. At about 40 minutes of accepted work plus $12 in review fees per credit, standing up 1,000 voting names costs roughly 667 hours and $12,000, and that spend must be repeated when the credits lapse.
